(Currently amended) Claim 1: A system for providing security in a computer system, the system comprising a **plurality of logic circuits each specifically configured to perform distinct operations, the plurality comprising at least a single logic circuit configured to:** receive a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seed a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generate a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and produce a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 2: The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of logic circuits includes at least one logic circuit configured to produce the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

(Cancelled) Claim 3

(Currently amended) Claim 4: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a ring oscillator, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the ring oscillator.

(Currently amended) Claim 5: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a single hardware source, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the single hardware source.

(Currently amended) Claim 6: The system of claim 1, wherein the hardware source is a plurality of independent hardware sources, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to receive the plurality of independent first entropy values from the plurality of independent hardware sources.

(Currently amended) Claim 7: The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a permutation function, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.

(Currently amended) Claim 8: The system of claim 7, wherein the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to: divide the plurality of independent first entropy values into multiple groups of independent first entropy values; apply the multiple groups of independent first entropy values to the permutation function to generate permuted groups of entropy values; and concatenate the permuted groups of entropy values to generate the second entropy value.

(Currently amended) Claim 9: The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a hash function, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the hash function.

(Currently amended) Claim 10: The system of claim 1, wherein the function is a bit-mixer, and the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the bit-mixer.

(Currently amended) Claim 11: The system of claim 1, wherein the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to selectively apply multiple entropy values of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function to generate the second entropy value.

(Currently amended) Claim 12: The system of claim 1, wherein the system includes at least one logic circuit specifically configured to apply at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values and a secret key to the function to generate the second entropy value.

(Currently amended) Claim 13: A method of providing security in a computer system, comprising: receiving a plurality of independent first entropy values from a hardware source; applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to a function to generate a second entropy value; seeding a pseudorandom number generator with the second entropy value; generating a random number using the pseudorandom number generator seeded with the second entropy value; and producing a block of ciphertext or message authentication code using the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 14: The method of claim 13, wherein producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code includes producing the block of ciphertext or message authentication code with a key composed of or derived from the random number.

(Currently amended) Claim 19: The method of claim 13, wherein the function is a permutation function, and wherein applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the function includes applying at least some of the plurality of independent first entropy values to the permutation function.
